claims.statement: Treat Telepathic’s initiative and status-phase timing as a round-five scoring advantage, not a reason to force an early Custodians grab.
claims.conditions: The hosts say acting first is awkward in early rounds and identify round five as the payoff; early Custodians is not recommended by default.
claims.compatibility: SCPT episode 270 (2022-10-26), discussing Codex 3 / Prophecy of Kings era; compatibility not independently rules-checked.
claims.uncertainty: Expected pace varies with game length, objectives, and table.

claims.statement: Naalu’s strong but thin position rewards restraint: bold offensive moves invite responses that may cost more than they gain.
claims.conditions: Especially before the fleet and economy are established; consider an aggressive line only when the gain warrants the attention and response risk.
claims.compatibility: SCPT episode 270 (2022-10-26), discussing Codex 3 / Prophecy of Kings era; compatibility not independently rules-checked.
claims.uncertainty: Table-specific strategic opinion.

claims.statement: Prioritize money and plastic before optional round-one technology; adding a carrier addresses the starting one-carrier bottleneck.
claims.conditions: When resources are tight; take tech early only if unusually wealthy and it does not displace useful units.
claims.compatibility: SCPT episode 270 (2022-10-26), discussing Codex 3 / Prophecy of Kings era; compatibility not independently rules-checked.
claims.uncertainty: Episode assumes Codex 3 agent-era kit.

claims.statement: Use Z’eu early to extend the starting carrier’s reach or perform a token-free non-home tactical action that fills out the slice.
claims.conditions: The player chosen performs a tactical action without placing a token, but that system still counts as activated; plan movement and follow-up.
claims.compatibility: SCPT episode 270 (2022-10-26), discussing Codex 3 / Prophecy of Kings era; compatibility not independently rules-checked.
claims.uncertainty: Episode’s verbal description is not full rules text.

claims.statement: A forward dock can make Z’eu a continuing production tool; place it where later ships matter and account for movement timing.
claims.conditions: After securing a forward dock, move again as needed before the dock locks the system.
claims.compatibility: SCPT episode 270 (2022-10-26), discussing Codex 3 / Prophecy of Kings era; compatibility not independently rules-checked.
claims.uncertainty: Round-one sequencing is discussed as awkward and situational.

claims.statement: Do not make Custodians an automatic round-two first action: an early bonus point attracts heat and may leave your slice or dock exposed.
claims.conditions: Take it if the table is already distributing early points or a safe line warrants the risk; otherwise another faction can take the spotlight.
claims.compatibility: SCPT episode 270 (2022-10-26), discussing Codex 3 / Prophecy of Kings era; compatibility not independently rules-checked.
claims.uncertainty: Recommendation, not a prohibition.

claims.statement: Reduce heat by making a rival more threatening than you; another player’s Custodians point can split attention and create a support-swap partner.
claims.conditions: Only boost a rival while monitoring their score; stop if they approach a win. The hosts warn that this political tactic can backfire.
claims.compatibility: SCPT episode 270 (2022-10-26), discussing Codex 3 / Prophecy of Kings era; compatibility not independently rules-checked.
claims.uncertainty: Boosting a rival can backfire.

claims.statement: Do not overvalue speaker just because Naalu act first; value it when it secures a specific later card plan.
claims.conditions: Politics may line up Imperial or an action-phase finish; taking it solely for Custodians timing is usually unnecessary.
claims.compatibility: SCPT episode 270 (2022-10-26), discussing Codex 3 / Prophecy of Kings era; compatibility not independently rules-checked.
claims.uncertainty: Card value depends on objectives and available picks.

claims.statement: Diplomacy is a strong round-one economic pick and helps counter the frustration of acting first in later rounds.
claims.conditions: Prefer it when planets and action order let you spend refreshed resources; speakers disagree about whether it beats Trade.
claims.compatibility: SCPT episode 270 (2022-10-26), discussing Codex 3 / Prophecy of Kings era; compatibility not independently rules-checked.
claims.uncertainty: Episode references a Codex 1 Diplomacy version.

claims.statement: Compare Trade and Diplomacy using the actual slice, neighbors, and primary/secondary value.
claims.conditions: Trade is attractive early if you can reach partners; its primary differs greatly from following its secondary, and another player’s Diplomacy can complement it.
claims.compatibility: SCPT episode 270 (2022-10-26), discussing Codex 3 / Prophecy of Kings era; compatibility not independently rules-checked.
claims.uncertainty: The source presents varying preferences and map dependencies.

claims.statement: Warfare is a round-one fallback for a second carrier, while its secondary may be more efficient if someone else takes it.
claims.conditions: If late pick and Warfare remains, one host favors taking it; the other argues Construction may be better because Z’eu eases movement.
claims.compatibility: SCPT episode 270 (2022-10-26), discussing Codex 3 / Prophecy of Kings era; compatibility not independently rules-checked.
claims.uncertainty: Hosts disagree on the no-Warfare table.

claims.statement: Construction matters if no one else will provide a forward dock; check whether you can afford to exploit it before preferring it to Diplomacy.
claims.conditions: Useful when a safe productive location exists; round-one cash and build timing can make the line awkward.
claims.compatibility: SCPT episode 270 (2022-10-26), discussing Codex 3 / Prophecy of Kings era; compatibility not independently rules-checked.
claims.uncertainty: Hosts disagree in late-pick cases.

claims.statement: Round-one Technology is less urgent than cash and units; Antimass or Dark Energy Tap can be useful, while Z’eu covers some early movement needs.
claims.conditions: Take Tech if the economy supports it or an objective specifically rewards the primary or secondary; consider asteroid access for Antimass.
claims.compatibility: SCPT episode 270 (2022-10-26), discussing Codex 3 / Prophecy of Kings era; compatibility not independently rules-checked.
claims.uncertainty: No objective legality/current-rules audit.

claims.statement: Build toward Hybrid Crystal Fighter II as the signature combat investment: the upgrade improves fighters and lets them move independently.
claims.conditions: Prioritize once resources and prerequisites allow; gather dispersed fighters for a late decisive maneuver.
claims.compatibility: SCPT episode 270 (2022-10-26), discussing Codex 3 / Prophecy of Kings era; compatibility not independently rules-checked.
claims.uncertainty: Hosts use emphatic comparisons; “better than War Suns” is rhetoric.

claims.statement: A stocked Hybrid Crystal Fighter II force can make a space attack on Naalu home look prohibitively costly.
claims.conditions: The hosts illustrate the deterrent with ten fighters; this is an anecdote, not a universal minimum, and it does not guarantee ground defense.
claims.compatibility: SCPT episode 270 (2022-10-26), discussing Codex 3 / Prophecy of Kings era; compatibility not independently rules-checked.
claims.uncertainty: The cited ten-fighter example is not a universal threshold.

claims.statement: Keep Neuroglaive optional rather than forcing a triple-green path: opponents can budget fleet tokens around its tax, while blue tech offers useful reach and tempo.
claims.conditions: Consider with convenient skips or when the table’s token economy makes the deterrent meaningful; do not expect it to stop coordinated win-slay.
claims.compatibility: SCPT episode 270 (2022-10-26), discussing Codex 3 / Prophecy of Kings era; compatibility not independently rules-checked.
claims.uncertainty: Hosts acknowledge some early-round deterrent potential.

claims.statement: Gravity Drive is useful for a late Matriarch or decisive reach, but the hosts do not recommend rushing it merely for early slice expansion.
claims.conditions: Acquire when it advances a concrete late move; Z’eu already covers some early movement needs.
claims.compatibility: SCPT episode 270 (2022-10-26), discussing Codex 3 / Prophecy of Kings era; compatibility not independently rules-checked.
claims.uncertainty: Assumes episode’s agent kit.

claims.statement: Treat Fleet Logistics as a finisher enabler, especially for a final-round Imperial line, rather than permission for repeated flashy double actions.
claims.conditions: Use when the extra action creates a decisive score or win-slay; consider acting first and giving opponents time to answer.
claims.compatibility: SCPT episode 270 (2022-10-26), discussing Codex 3 / Prophecy of Kings era; compatibility not independently rules-checked.
claims.uncertainty: Hosts warn against overuse but acknowledge strong specific lines.

claims.statement: Z’eu can enable an allied attack or win-slay; consider selling its use when that changes who can stop the leader.
claims.conditions: Compare the deal with your own need for its build or movement action; the hosts say its price and value vary.
claims.compatibility: SCPT episode 270 (2022-10-26), discussing Codex 3 / Prophecy of Kings era; compatibility not independently rules-checked.
claims.uncertainty: No unconditional sale value implied.

claims.statement: Foresight is an emergency pre-combat escape that costs a strategy-pool token; reserve it for fights that must be avoided or positions worth preserving.
claims.conditions: It may deny a secret or preserve ships, but a normal retreat can be better when the token is needed for a secondary.
claims.compatibility: SCPT episode 270 (2022-10-26), discussing Codex 3 / Prophecy of Kings era; compatibility not independently rules-checked.
claims.uncertainty: Hosts differ about whether the unusual Mecatol use justifies the cost.

claims.statement: The Matriarch combines capacity and invasion flexibility: carry a real ground force to start combat, then commit fighters as temporary ground combatants.
claims.conditions: Strong for a late offensive swing; plan how to defend the planet after fighters return to space.
claims.compatibility: SCPT episode 270 (2022-10-26), discussing Codex 3 / Prophecy of Kings era; compatibility not independently rules-checked.
claims.uncertainty: Informal explanation; no separate rules audit.

claims.statement: Pair a mech with fighters where anti-fighter barrage threatens the fleet; the episode describes Iconoclast Omega as shutting off that interaction in its system.
claims.conditions: Relevant against Argent or Destroyer II plans and when Matriarch needs a lone invader.
claims.compatibility: SCPT episode 270 (2022-10-26), discussing Codex 3 / Prophecy of Kings era; compatibility not independently rules-checked.
claims.uncertainty: Codex/Omega/TE-era variants exist; edition must be resolved.

claims.statement: M’aban’s described Omega unlock requires ground forces in or adjacent to Mecatol Rex; the hosts say Z’eu plus a nearby planet can make the unlock possible in round one.
claims.conditions: This route depends on the map providing the necessary nearby planets and on the discussed Omega commander version.
claims.compatibility: SCPT episode 270 (2022-10-26), discussing Codex 3 / Prophecy of Kings era; compatibility not independently rules-checked.
claims.uncertainty: ASR renders Mecatol as “mek atoll”; the intended name is clear in context, but the ability/version is not independently rules-checked.

claims.statement: Use M’aban’s agenda peek for planning, and wait until another agenda ability fully resolves before checking again.
claims.conditions: The hosts value agenda information more than inspecting neighbors’ promissory notes in routine high-level play.
claims.compatibility: SCPT episode 270 (2022-10-26), discussing Codex 3 / Prophecy of Kings era; compatibility not independently rules-checked.
claims.uncertainty: Some interface details are TTPG-specific.

claims.statement: The Oracle hero is low-value on average; use it promptly because earlier forced promissory notes are more likely to matter.
claims.conditions: Political secrets may be a strong result; late Trade Agreements or weak alliances may be worth little.
claims.compatibility: SCPT episode 270 (2022-10-26), discussing Codex 3 / Prophecy of Kings era; compatibility not independently rules-checked.
claims.uncertainty: Hosts give edge cases, not a dependable outcome.

claims.statement: Keep Gift of Prescience: its temporary initiative advantage disables Telepathic that round, and the hosts see little reason to trade away Naalu’s defining tempo tool.
claims.conditions: Avoid Custodians-sale lines based on old early-game assumptions; Z’eu now creates other movement and deal options.
claims.compatibility: SCPT episode 270 (2022-10-26), discussing Codex 3 / Prophecy of Kings era; compatibility not independently rules-checked.
claims.uncertainty: Discussion explicitly contrasts older pre-PoK thinking with the agent-era view; text’s return timing may be base-game context.

claims.statement: Use Z’eu and a strong air fleet for late win-slay plans, but consider saving the agent instead of spending it on an early build.
claims.conditions: In rounds four and five, track rivals’ action-phase win lines and retain enough movement and ships to intervene.
claims.compatibility: SCPT episode 270 (2022-10-26), discussing Codex 3 / Prophecy of Kings era; compatibility not independently rules-checked.
claims.uncertainty: Naalu can also lose by waiting while another rival wins first.

claims.statement: Plan round-four/five scoring from revealed objectives and secret progress; a stage-two flip or late Imperial point can turn a quiet game into a win.
claims.conditions: Choose between status-phase scoring and action-phase finish using the table’s actual pace; do not assume the round-five point is victory if someone can win sooner.
claims.compatibility: SCPT episode 270 (2022-10-26), discussing Codex 3 / Prophecy of Kings era; compatibility not independently rules-checked.
claims.uncertainty: Tempo advantage is not guaranteed victory.

connections.conditions: The chosen tactical action moves the fleet without adding a command token and can extend the carrier route.
The Matriarch lets fighters join an invasion as ground combatants, then returns them to space.
Iconoclast is described as preventing anti-fighter barrage in its system, protecting the fighter force.
Construction can place the forward dock that Z’eu later activates for production.
Gravity Drive supports the late Matriarch movement described by the hosts.
Gift of Prescience gives its holder first initiative while disabling Telepathic for that round.
